input:
This passage reviews the cost of a regional delivery route. The route covers 784 km per trip, and the cost is $1.54 per km, with a total of 836 trips per year. On this basis, the annual transport cost works out at $1009k. The costs are taken from carrier invoices for the last 12 months, so they represent the amounts actually invoiced rather than estimates.

It is worth noting that empty running is included in the trip count, which means that the annual figure of $1009k covers all of the trips that were made during the year, both loaded and empty. This is an important point to bear in mind when the figure is used, because it means that the cost cannot simply be attributed to loaded deliveries alone, and comparisons with other figures need to be made on a like-for-like basis.

Overall, the review establishes the annual cost of the route on a consistent basis, and this figure can be used as the starting point for considering any changes to the route or to the arrangements with the carrier in the future.

It should also be understood that the annual figure combines two rather different drivers, namely the distance covered on each trip and the number of trips that are made in the year, and the review does not attempt to separate the contribution of each of these drivers to the total that has been reported.
target:
Annual transport cost on the regional delivery route is $1009k. The figure is derived from the route's operating numbers: 784 km per trip, at $1.54 per km, over 836 trips per year. Costs are carrier invoices for the last 12 months, so the figure is invoiced cost, not an estimate built from rates alone.

Empty running is included in the trip count. The cost therefore stands against all invoiced trips, loaded and empty together, and no part of the $1009k is assigned to loaded running alone; a cost per loaded trip would need the loaded share of the count, which the invoices do not separate. The rate is likewise a blended figure: it averages the trips the route actually ran, at the distances they actually covered, and it moves if either the trip pattern or the carrier's pricing moves.

The review covers the transport leg only. It states what the route cost over the year on a consistent trip definition, which is the figure any change to the route, the vehicle or the carrier is costed against. Comparisons with earlier periods hold only where the trip count was kept on the same basis, empty running included; a period counted on loaded trips alone would show a lower cost for the same operation.

The figure is a cost of record for one route over one year. It does not separate the cost of distance from the cost of frequency: a route run less often at the same distance, or over a shorter distance at the same frequency, would present a different total through a different term, and the review does not rank the two levers against each other.
